title: Info for Spectators — Boston Marathon
claims: Hopkinton has been home to the start line since 1924.
The spectator page describes the course as point to point and advises spectators who want to see a runner in multiple places to plan carefully.

Town-by-town mile ranges are Hopkinton start–1.90, Ashland 1.90–4.95, Framingham 4.95–7.52, Natick 7.52–11.72, Wellesley 11.72–15.93, Newton 15.93–21.35, Boston 21.35–22.45 and 24.70–26.20, and Brookline 22.45–24.70.
The road-closure table lists Hopkinton 7:00 a.m.–1:30 p.m., Ashland 7:00–1:45, Framingham 7:45–2:15, Natick 8:30–3:00, Wellesley 8:30–4:15, Newton 8:00–5:30, Brookline 9:00–6:00 and Boston 9:00–7:00.
The town-by-town section gives different closure times for some towns, including Framingham 7:30–2:15, Wellesley 8:00–3:35 and Brookline 8:00–6:00.

MBTA Commuter Rail stops named are Ashland, Framingham, West Natick, Natick Center, Wellesley Square, Wellesley Hills and Wellesley Farms; Green Line access includes Woodland, Boston College and Cleveland Circle.
The Newton Hills are described as miles 17.5 to 21.
The Wellesley Scream Tunnel near Wellesley College is described as just before the halfway point.
The Family Meeting Area is on Stuart Street between Berkeley and Clarendon Streets.
Suggested Boston garages are 100 Clarendon, Prudential Center, Copley Place and Boston Common Garage, with Boston Common Garage closed on Marathon Monday morning.
A sensory-friendly viewing area is at the Tolles Parsons Center, 500 Washington Street, Wellesley, around mile 13.5.
The course is a No-Drone Zone and spectators may not enter the course or pace a runner.
The B.A.A. states that, for public safety, the route may be changed and the race may be paused or cancelled before or during the event.
Hynes Convention Center station is noted as not suitable for accessible use.
